teams.heading: Borthwick restores George Furbank at full-back as Fin Smith passes fitness test
teams.body: Fin Smith has been deemed fit to face Australia after a build-up injury scare, and has started England's past five matches, usurping George Ford in the process. George Furbank has been out of the Test side since November 2024, with injuries and an appendicitis bout in the July window keeping him away. Greg Fisilau, the Exeter Chiefs back-rower, is in the matchday squad and in line for a maiden cap.

lead.why: A fresh England selection story with named players, which beats the rehashed rift row and the opinion pieces.

teams.heading: France have won three of their last five, most recently against Japan
teams.body: Across their last five matches, France have won three and lost two, with results running win, win, loss, win, loss, most recent first. Their current run is two straight wins, and the latest of them was a 42-15 victory away to Japan, which was Round 3 of the Nations Championship Group Stage in July. In that group they have played three, won two and lost one.

teams.heading: Ireland injury list grows after Dan Sheehan fails head injury assessment against Argentina
teams.body: Sheehan was taken off in the first half of Friday's 42-12 win after failing a head injury assessment, though Andy Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room". Robert Baloucoune also left with a knock, going off in the 58th minute, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee. Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns, and Hansen continued after treatment. Those two were part of a back three that had only played together once before, four years ago against South Africa.

lead.why: It is a new team-news story, with Dan Sheehan's head injury assessment and several knocks to Ireland's players, and it is corroborated by two outlets.

teams.heading: Quesada's injury-hit Azzurri lose 66-7 to Springboks in Turin on Saturday
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada named Giacomo Nicotera captain for the Turin match, with Michele Lamaro out, and the side were also missing centres Tommaso Menoncello and Nacho Brex. The Springboks won 66-7, and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu scored an early try in the eighth minute. Brex expects surgery on a detached bicep next week, and Menoncello faces 12 weeks out after a shoulder injury. Italy remain without a win after four matches, with Argentina next up in Round 5.

teams.heading: Andrew Brace referees Scotland v All Blacks after recent Furlong grab incident
teams.body: Andrew Brace, a 38-year-old IRFU official who has worked two Rugby World Cups, takes charge of Saturday's Test at Murrayfield. He was refereeing Leinster v Munster when Gavin Coombes reported that his groin had been grabbed in a ruck, and Tadhg Furlong was cited for allegedly grabbing him. Brace referred the incident to TMO Colin Stanley, but the broadcast angles were inconclusive and no penalty or card followed. Furlong was later found not guilty by the citing commission.

lead.why: It is the freshest item tied directly to Scotland's Saturday Test, and it concerns the match official.

teams.heading: Bill Sweeney confirms WRU's bid to put Welsh clubs into the PREM
teams.body: The RFU has received a formal request from the Welsh Rugby Union to bring Welsh clubs into the Gallagher PREM. Chief executive Bill Sweeney told BBC Radio Four the request had been put in writing, that the RFU would go back with questions, and that its focus remains on expanding the English game. The United Rugby Championship has meanwhile threatened the WRU, a shareholder, with legal action over plans to leave the competition.

lead.why: It is a fresh formal development in Welsh union business, with the RFU confirming a WRU request to bring Welsh clubs into the PREM, rather than a repeat of the Mann or lineup stories already covered.

teams.heading: Argentina Legends open World Rugby Classic title defence against Italian Classic XV
teams.body: The Legends, seeking an eighth title, want early league points before a week that also takes them to France Classic Rugby on Tuesday and the Classic Lions on Friday. Last year they won the trophy with a 13-7 victory over the Classic Springboks. Tournament president John Kane said "Argentina will be favourites and the Lions will be second favourites." The match is part of the 38th edition of the tournament.

lead.why: It is a fresh Argentina fixture story in the pack, and it is clearly a different story from the Ireland defeat already covered.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight to earn 50th cap as Jeremy Williams starts at six
teams.body: Fraser McReight will earn his 50th cap for Australia against England at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, forming a new-look back row with Jeremy Williams at blindside flanker and Harry Wilson, who captains the side again from number eight. Len Ikitau returns to midfield after missing the last Test under HIA protocols, alongside Isaac Henry, who plays his first Test in the United Kingdom. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is back at the venue of his 2024 Test debut, on the right wing.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones starts uncapped Riku Kitahara at fly-half against Wales
teams.body: Riku Kitahara, the Honda Heat fly-half, has been picked to start in Cardiff, with Shinya Komura on the bench as Japan's only other fly-half option on tour. Kitahara has not yet won a cap. The selection comes with Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee both injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who has started all of Japan's Tests in 2026, back at university and missing the entire tour.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson says Richie Mo'unga misses Scotland clash as Barrett's form grows
teams.body: Dave Rennie's 10-and-15 picture is tightening. Jeff Wilson told Sport Nation that Richie Mo'unga, who is targeting Wales, will not be available for the Scotland match. Beauden Barrett, 35, has moved into the 15 jersey and is dovetailing with Damian McKenzie at 10, a pairing retained for the Nations Championship opener. Wilson says Barrett's form could give the selectors headaches, since McKenzie was Rennie's preferred 15 before the Bledisloe Cup. Ruben Love's return next season is also a factor.

lead.why: It is the only new item with a team-news fact (Richie Mo'unga unavailable this week) and a selection question for Dave Rennie.

teams.heading: Mzwandile Stick says Springboks will go all out in remaining Tests
teams.body: Assistant coach Mzwandile Stick told the media on Friday, before the 66-7 win over Italy, that the Springboks are determined to win each of their remaining Tests. He said there is no room to ease off, with the All Blacks also chasing every win. On injuries, Stick said the squad had depth to cope: "So if there are injuries, we know one thing for sure: the other guys will be ready." The Boks still have Ireland in Dublin and France in Paris before the finals weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: A fresh press-conference comment from a Springboks coach on the remaining Tests and squad depth, which is a South Africa story rather than a rival's view or a backward-looking match report.
